newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 14.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 14. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto has asked the Indonesian Textile Association (API) to help the authorities combat textile smuggling. API officials said textile was being smuggled into Indonesia which affected the domestic market.
The economic advisory group Econit suggested the government review its mining contract policy because it was outdated and failed to generate the greatest possible benefits for Indonesians.

Guruh Sukarnoputra, a senior member of the divided Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said he would not campaign for any of the three political parties contesting the general election in May. Guruh is the youngest son of Indonesia's first president Sukarno.

Indonesia's largest Moslem organisation Nahdlatul Ulama said it was not involved in last month's riots in Tasikmalaya, West Java, where a mob of mainly Moslem youth went on a rampage, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches. Four people died in the disturbance.
The government has presented a bill at the House of Representatives which aims to regulate non-tax revenue.
